toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Dikwels' appears three times in this short block; 'baie keer' means the same and keeps the qualifier while varying the wording.
toegepas.fout: 'dikwels' appears three times in a seven-sentence block, which a careful reader notices
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Baie keer' is plain spoken Afrikaans, keeps the same qualifier and breaks the repetition without moving the meaning.

laat_vaar.voor: Die dans is na daardie stewels genoem
laat_vaar.na: Die dans is na daardie stewels vernoem
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Na iets genoem' calques English 'named after'; the Afrikaans idiom is 'na iets vernoem'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Na iets genoem' is ordinary, correct Afrikaans (as in 'n kind na sy oupa noem), not a calque, so 'vernoem' is a lateral swap.

laat_vaar.blok: Gumboot-dans: hoe dit lyk en klink
laat_vaar.voor: volg die span dikwels die maat
laat_vaar.na: volg die span dikwels die ritme
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Die maat volg' can be read as 'follow the partner', since the glossary uses 'maat' for a partner; 'ritme' is the lesson's own word for the beat and keeps the meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Die maat volg' is the fixed musical expression for keeping time to the musicians' beat, and changing it to 'ritme' swaps a term of art and moves the meaning in a lesson that sets the dancers' own rhythm against the music.

laat_vaar.voor: Dit is die klem en nie
laat_vaar.na: Dit is elke dans se klem en nie
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The bare 'Dit' has no clear referent after two sentences about two dances; naming whose emphasis it is makes the reference clear without adding content.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: In context 'Dit is die klem' clearly refers to the two contrasts just named, and 'elke dans se klem' can be misread as a claim about every dance in general.

na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'n Dans dans' repeats the same word as noun and verb and reads clumsily; the passive says the same thing smoothly.
na_skrywer.fout: 'n dans dans' repeats the word as noun and verb and reads clumsily
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: This rewords a glossary definition beyond a spelling or grammar fix, and the passive also drops 'mense', so the writer should decide the wording for every lesson that uses it.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

na_skrywer.na: soos daardie karakter dit sou doen.
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: Ending on the bare modal 'sou' copies English 'as that character would'; Afrikaans completes the verb phrase.
na_skrywer.fout: the definition ends on a bare 'sou', which copies English 'as that character would'
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The fault is real, but it sits in a glossary definition that may only be reworded through the writer.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.blok: Drie punte om na 'n dans te kyk
vlae.teks: hoe die liggaam beweeg en waarop gedans word
vlae.rede: 'Waarop gedans word' can be read as the surface danced on rather than the music danced to; the later block says 'die musiek waarop hulle dans', but which is meant here cannot be fixed without guessing the intended content.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Langs mekaar wys die drie punte hoe verskillend die twee danse is.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Die drie punte wys hoe verskillend die twee danse langs mekaar is.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: As written, 'langs mekaar' attaches to the three points rather than the two dances; the reorder fixes the reference without adding words.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The fronted 'Langs mekaar' reads naturally and echoes the heading; the reorder is a lateral move that now suggests the dances stand physically side by side.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Dit is die klem en nie die enigste
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Dit is die klem, nie die enigste
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'en nie' makes the contrast read like an addition; a comma states the contrast directly and saves a word.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Dit is die klem en nie die enigste ...' is ordinary natural Afrikaans; the comma version is only different.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Opgemaakte' echoes English 'made-up'; 'versinde' is the standard Afrikaans word.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Opgemaakte' is established, plain Afrikaans (as in 'n opgemaakte storie'), while 'versinde' is harder for a Grade 5 reader and rewords a glossary definition for no clear gain.
